event.t: The US, Russia and Ukraine met in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, their first three-way talks since February.
Delegations were led by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for the US, Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky for Russia, and Rustem Umerov for Ukraine.
Talks focused on security guarantees for Ukraine and Europe, Russia’s own security demands, de-escalation and prisoners.
Main result: agreement on a prisoner exchange. Ukraine’s negotiator says significant differences remain.
On 12 November the US envoys met Putin in Moscow, then Zelensky in Dublin. Kushner said Russia and Ukraine agreed that European countries will join the next round of talks.
Zelensky and Kushner both say the prisoner exchange would be the largest of the war. The reports give no date for it.

next.t: The prisoner exchange, and a next round of talks that includes European countries. The reports so far give no dates.

event.t: The summit’s second and final week began on Monday 16 November. Ministers now have to settle what negotiators could not.

A first draft of the main summit text was published on Monday 16 November. It calls for faster action to move away from coal, oil and gas, and asks countries to raise electricity to 35% of final energy use by 2035. Nearly 200 countries still have to approve it.
Countries are divided on whether to have a cover decision at all, and on what should be in it.
Host Türkiye wants a goal to raise electricity to 35% of the world’s energy use by 2035. Several large developing countries reject new targets for single sectors in the text.

On money, developing countries want a promise of at least $120 billion a year by 2035 to help them adapt to climate change, Climate Home News reports. Richer countries have offered little new finance so far.

event.t: On Sunday 15 November, Bahrain said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian air attacks before they reached their targets. Sirens and explosions were reported across the country.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a US military base in Bahrain in response to what they called hostile US actions. Iranian state media said six drones were aimed at a US air-defence radar at a helicopter base.

It is the second such claim in three days. On 13 November the Guards said they had hit a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. The US military denied this and said it shot down two drones with no damage.
It is the first time since September that Bahrain’s air defences have had to stop attacks like this.

There is still no deal to end the war. Reuters reported on Saturday that President Trump has said he might hold off from attacking Iran if there are no new provocations, while keeping the US naval blockade.

event.t: Brent was down 47 cents, or 0.49%, at $95.37 a barrel at 01:45 GMT on Monday 16 November. US crude (WTI) was down 0.26% at $88.33.
Reuters says prices fell because traders expect a supply surplus: shipments from the Middle East through the Strait of Hormuz are almost back to pre-war levels.
Brent settled at $95.84 on Friday 13 November. That was about 2.5% lower than a week earlier ($98.32 on 6 November) and its second weekly fall in a row.
The International Energy Agency expects the oil market to move back into surplus. More oil from its members’ emergency reserves is still due to reach the market.
Prices can still jump on war news: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday that they attacked a US base in Bahrain.

event.t: The official campaign began on Friday 13 November and runs until 27 November. Voting is on Sunday 29 November.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called the early vote on 5 October, after parliament rejected his government’s emergency housing measures.
Most private polls put the conservative People’s Party (PP) first. They give PP and Vox together about 190 to 200 of the 350 seats; 176 are needed for a majority.

The state polling institute, the CIS, shows a different picture: Socialists first on 33.3%, PP on 25.5% and Vox on 18.4%, leaving PP and Vox short of a majority. It has differed from private polls before.
A high-speed train crash that killed 69 people on 28 October changed the campaign. Transport minister Óscar Puente resigned six days later.
The main issues are the cost of housing, immigration, corruption allegations and rail safety.

stories.sh: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in China
stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin are due to hold their first three-way meeting in China on Thursday
stories.summary: The leaders of the US, China and Russia are due to meet together for the first time on Thursday 19 November, in Shenzhen, during the APEC summit. The White House says the main topic is reducing nuclear weapons.
stories.why: The US, Russia and China are the world’s biggest nuclear powers, and their three leaders have never met as a group. What they agree, or fail to agree, could shape arms control for years. The meeting also comes while the wars in Ukraine and Iran are still going on.
stories.simple: The presidents of the United States, China and Russia plan to sit down together on Thursday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. It would be the first time the three meet as a group. The US says it wants to talk about having fewer nuclear weapons.

event.t: The White House said on Friday 13 November that President Trump will meet China’s leader Xi Jinping and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin together. It would be the first three-way meeting of the countries’ leaders.
The Kremlin said the meeting will be held on 19 November in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. China’s foreign ministry confirmed the place and the day on Monday 16 November.
The White House says Trump wants to discuss reducing the number of nuclear weapons in the world.
US officials told ABC News that Trump expects to discuss Iran with Xi and Putin, but does not plan to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine at the three-way meeting.

effects.label: Arms control
effects.t: A joint commitment on nuclear weapons by the three powers would be new. No three-way agreement of this kind exists today.

effects.label: Ukraine
effects.t: The war is not on the agenda of the three-way meeting, US officials told ABC News. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera say the meeting lets Putin show strength while the war is set aside.

effects.label: Iran
effects.t: Trump is expected to raise Iran with Xi and Putin, according to US officials.

fr.A first draft of the summit’s main text: Un premier projet du texte principal du sommet est publié. Il appelle à accélérer la sortie du charbon, du pétrole et du gaz, et à porter l’électricité à 35 % de la consommation finale d’énergie d’ici à 2035. Près de 200 pays doivent encore l’approuver.
fr.The draft is the basis for the bargainin: Ce projet sert de base aux tractations avant l’échéance de vendredi.

fr.Two candidates are nominated to succeed: Deux candidats sont proposés pour succéder à Christine Lagarde : l’Espagnol Pablo Hernández de Cos et le Néerlandais Klaas Knot. fr.The winner will lead the ECB’s interest: Le candidat retenu conduira les décisions de la BCE sur les taux d’intérêt après le départ de Lagarde, le 7 février 2027.
fr.In speeches during the week, Fed officia: Dans leurs discours de la semaine, des responsables de la Fed laissent attendre une hausse des taux en décembre. Le gouverneur Christopher Waller dit qu’une hausse d’un demi-point devrait être envisagée, soit le double du pas habituel.
fr.A larger rise would be a stronger move a: Une hausse plus forte serait un geste plus ferme contre l’inflation que le quart de point habituel.

fr.AP’s count as of Nov 16, 12:15pm CET sho: Le décompte d’AP au 16 novembre à 12 h 15 (heure d’Europe centrale) donne 256 sièges à la Chambre remportés par les démocrates et 169 par les républicains. Au Sénat, le décompte d’AP au 16 novembre à 12 h 14 (heure d’Europe centrale) donne un total de 55 sièges pour les démocrates et 44 pour les républicains. Dans ces résultats, 1 siège du Sénat n’est compté comme remporté ou conservé par aucun des deux partis ; ils ne disent pas non plus pourquoi ni de quel côté il ira. Ces chiffres ont pu changer depuis.
